about: Hand-written orders with borderline cases. The answers are labelled from the rule definitions in docs/architecture/rules.md, not produced by running the engine. Synthetic data.

cases.why: retry exactly 24 h after the failure: inclusive window, so a retry
retry 24 h and one second after the failure: fallout
failed on a transient code and never retried: fallout
permanent error code: a retry cannot fix it, not fallout
failed inside the declared maintenance window: expected, not fallout
failed exactly at the end of the maintenance window: the window includes its end
failed one second after the maintenance window: fallout
error code the client never classified: counted as fallout, flagged unknown
two failures 10 h apart and then nothing: the first was retried, the second not; one order counted once
the service order was cancelled: a failure there is not fallout
the activation failed and a new service order over the same item succeeded an hour later: a retry for R01, a duplicate (retry_new_order) for R04
a pending attempt is not a failure
legitimate retry two hours after the failure
two orders share a terminal serial (see ORD-V15)
an attempt that carries only the shared serial fits two service orders: ambiguous, one weak link, placed under no order
an attempt with only a unique serial joins by inference: one weak link
a failed attempt joined only by serial and never retried: fallout on a weak link
replaced by ORD-V18B (an amendment); shares its terminal
amendment: the attempt that carries only the shared serial belongs to the replacement, one weak link and no ambiguity
the failure is written +02:00 (21:30Z); a retry 24 h 15 min later is fallout, though read as UTC the gap would look like 22 h 15 min
the failure is written -05:00 (06:00Z); a retry 23 h 30 min later is a retry, though read as UTC the gap would look like 28 h 30 min
timer expired exactly 72 h before the end of the period: not yet stuck
timer expired 72 h and one second before the end: stuck
timer expired and a person ran activation_recovery: recovered
timer expired and an open fallout_review task owns it: in human management
timer expired but the process is suspended on purpose
timer expired and the process went on with another task, then ended
a timer that did not expire is a healthy wait
an expired timer that is not in timer_activities is not watched
a plan change (modify) over the item of an added service: an amendment, not a duplicate
the first service order was cancelled and a new one replaced it: deliberate, not a duplicate
a process that only carries the business key: one inferred link
nothing wrong: one service order, one successful attempt, one finished process
